title: Seating Arrangement
why_it_matters: Seating arrangement tests logical placement under multiple constraints. It appears in TCS NQT and Infosys reasoning sections.

misconceptions.signature: Student freezes the first mentioned person and ignores facing direction.
Student ignores 'to the left of' when building the arrangement.

captain_byte.intro: Seating arrangement is a logic grid. Fix one reference, then place everyone relative to it.
captain_byte.after_break: You found the placement error. Now rebuild the arrangement from the fixed reference.
captain_byte.after_mastery: You can now solve seating arrangements fast. That's placement-ready reasoning skill.
captain_byte.retry_prompt: Try again. Fix one reference person and facing direction first.

steps.narration: A, B, C sit in a line. A is left of B. B is left of C. Order?

interaction.explanation: A left of B, B left of C → A-B-C.

steps.narration: If they face north, 'left of' means west from each person's view.

interaction.prompt: Facing north, A is left of B. Where is A?

discover.conclusion: Fix one reference. Place others relative to it. Left/right depends on facing direction. Check all constraints before finalizing.

understand: Seating arrangements use relative positions: left, right, opposite, between, next to. Facing direction changes left/right. Circular arrangements wrap around. Linear arrangements have ends.

manipulate.prompt: A, B, C sit in a line. A is between B and C. B is at the left end. Order?
manipulate.hint: B is fixed at left. A is between B and C → B-A-C.

predict.prompt: Four people sit around a table. A is right of B. C is opposite D. Who is left of A?

build.prompt: Arrange A, B, C, D in a line. A is left of B. C is between A and D. D is at the right end.
build.explanation: D fixed at right. C between A and D. A left of B.

break_step.prompt: A student places A left of B as A on the left side of the page. What is wrong?
break_step.common_mistake: Confusing viewer's left/right with the person's left/right when facing direction is not fixed.
break_step.correct_reasoning: Left/right depends on facing direction. Fix facing first.

debug.prompt: Fix: 'A is left of B' when facing south.

transfer.prompt: Five people sit in a line. P is left of Q. R is between P and S. T is at the right end. Order?
transfer.explanation: T fixed right. R between P and S. P left of Q.

practice.prompt: A is between B and C. B is left of A. Order?
practice.explanation: B left of A, A between B and C → B-A-C.

practice.prompt: Four people face north. A is right of B. Who is left of B?
practice.explanation: Only one relation given; not enough to determine all positions.

practice.prompt: Practice 1: Apply Seating Arrangement to solve this problem.
practice.explanation: This demonstrates Seating Arrangement in a placement context.

proof.prompt: Six people sit in a circle. A is opposite B. C is left of A. D is right of B. Find positions of C and D relative to A.
proof.correct: C is left of A; D is right of B
proof.explanation: Use fixed reference A and relative directions.

proof.prompt: Prove your Seating Arrangement skill: explain the solution to this problem.
proof.explanation: This tests understanding of Seating Arrangement.

proof_questions.prompt: TCS: A, B, C, D sit in a line facing north. B is at one end. C is between A and D. Who is second from left?
proof_questions.explanation: B at end, C between A and D → B-C-A-D or B-A-C-D depending on constraints.

srs_key_points: Fix one reference person and facing direction.
